ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a corner of a floor, with the upper boundary and left boundary as solid lines, and inside there is an equally spaced dashed-line grid; the distance between adjacent dashed lines can be regarded as 1 unit. The darker gray pattern is composed of edges along grid lines and 45-degree diagonal edges; from the figure it can be seen that the gray pattern repeats every 6 units in both the horizontal and vertical directions, and a complete 6×6 repeating block may be taken at the upper-left corner. Reasoning: In this 6×6 repeating block, decomposing and counting by the 6 horizontal unit strips from top to bottom, the gray areas are respectively 1, 2, 5, 5, 2, 1 unit squares, and the total gray area is 1+2+5+5+2+1=16. The area of the whole repeating block is 6×6=36. The problem states that the whole floor is paved in the same way, and all four corners are like this figure, so the side length of the floor aligns with the repeating period and will not leave incomplete edge periods. Thus the proportion of the dark part in the whole floor equals the proportion in one repeating block, namely 16/36=4/9.

method.method_draft: Use a translational-period area count. From the image, first read the dashed square lattice as unit grid lines and note that the gray polygonal pattern repeats after 6 grid intervals horizontally and vertically; the visible top-left corner gives one complete 6-by-6 repeat block. Count the gray area inside that 6-by-6 block by decomposing along the grid lines and the 45-degree diagonal cuts, for example by summing the gray areas in the six horizontal unit strips as 1, 2, 5, 5, 2, and 1 unit-square areas, for a total of 16 dark unit squares out of 36. From the text, use that the whole floor is tiled in this same way and that all four corners look like the shown corner, so the floor dimensions contain whole repeat blocks with no unmatched partial-period edge. Apply the periodic-density rule: the fraction of the whole floor that is dark equals the fraction in one repeat block, so 16/36 = 4/9.
